_partNote: The trap on this sheet is drawing a wafer seven times, so each class gets the object that belongs to its stage instead: a grown ingot, a square mask plate, a layered slab with etched holes, a single packaged die, a compound wafer with flats, a stepped die stack, and a probe card. Only two are discs, and those two differ in thickness, edge shape, and what sits on the face.

partPrompts.1: A single-crystal ingot lying horizontally on a flat surface, seen three-quarter: a long heavy cylinder about four times as long as it is wide, one end tapering to a blunt cone and the other cut square, with one long flat ground down the length of its side. The tapered end and the ground flat are what identify it. One object on a plain surface, no wafers, no discs, no machine.
partPrompts.2: A square photomask plate lying flat, seen three-quarter: a thick slab of glass, clearly much thicker than a wafer, with one plain rectangular patterned field centered on its upper face and a thin rectangular membrane frame standing a short distance above that face on four short corner posts. Square, not round: no disc, no notch, no edge flat, no fine markings, no light rays and no machine.
partPrompts.3: A small rectangular slab standing on a flat surface, seen three-quarter, its front vertical face built of about fifteen thin horizontal layers stacked like a layer cake, each layer the same thickness and running the full width. Three or four deep narrow round holes drop straight down from the top face into the stack. One object on a plain surface; not a wafer, not a disc, no chamber and no machine.
partPrompts.4: One thin square die lying centered on a larger square substrate, seen three-quarter: a low flat two-piece stack, the die noticeably smaller than the board beneath it and set square to its edges, with a regular grid of small round bumps along the visible underside edge of the substrate. Exactly one die and one tier, nothing stacked on top of it, no lid, no wires, no machine.
partPrompts.5: A round wafer lying flat on a plain surface, seen three-quarter: a disc with one long straight flat cut across its edge and a second shorter flat at right angles to it, its face plain and mirror-smooth with no pattern on it at all. Clearly a smaller and thicker disc than a full-size wafer. Not a notch, not a grid of dies, one object with no machine.
partPrompts.6: A staircase stack of four thin square dies sitting on a larger flat square base, seen three-quarter, each die stepped back from the one below so all four tiers are visible from the side. Beside the stack, on the same base and well clear of it, lies one single low flat die. The tiered staircase is the subject; no lid, no heat spreader, no wires and no machine.
partPrompts.7: A probe card held horizontally, seen three-quarter from slightly below: a thick round circuit board with a raised stiffener ring around its rim, and a dense cluster of very fine straight needles projecting down from the middle of its underside, angling inward to a small square footprint below the board. The downward needle cluster is the subject. A thick board rather than a thin polished wafer, with nothing underneath it and no machine.
